source_fact_en: Brachytherapy places a radiation source inside or near the cancer through a catheter or applicator.
Before brachytherapy begins you may have a planning visit with a physical exam medical history review and imaging tests.
Once the catheter or applicator is in place the radiation source is inserted for the planned treatment time.
Low-dose-rate brachytherapy may stay in place for 1 to 7 days while high-dose-rate treatment is usually given for 10 to 20 minutes at a time.
After LDR or HDR treatment the treated area may stay tender for a while even though no radiation remains in your body after the catheter is removed.
Chemotherapy uses drugs to kill cancer cells or stop them from growing.
Chemotherapy may be used before surgery or radiation to shrink a tumor.
Chemotherapy may also be used after surgery or radiation to destroy cancer cells that remain.
Chemotherapy can damage fast-growing healthy cells too, so side effects may include mouth sores nausea hair loss and fatigue.
If chemotherapy leaves you very tired plan time to rest and ask for help with meals or rides.
Chemotherapy may be given by mouth through a vein by injection into the skin or muscle or by other specialized routes.
IV chemotherapy is often delivered through a thin needle in a vein and sometimes through a catheter or port.
Cervical cancer treatment may involve more than one type of therapy and the plan depends on stage overall health and personal preferences.
If you are worried about fertility ask your cancer care team about it before cervical cancer treatment begins.
Chemotherapy for cervical cancer may be given alone or together with other treatments.
After cervical cancer treatment follow-up visits are often scheduled every 3 to 4 months for the first 2 years and then every 6 months.
Cervical cancer screening aims to find precancerous cell changes before cancer develops or spreads.
The three main cervical screening approaches are the HPV test the Pap test and the HPV/Pap cotest.
For people ages 21 to 29 the USPSTF recommends starting Pap testing at age 21 and repeating it every 3 years.
Even if you have had HPV vaccination you still need to follow cervical cancer screening recommendations.
Palliative care focuses on improving quality of life and can be given together with curative cancer treatment.

source_title: Definition of palliative care - NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms - NCI
source_fact_en: Palliative care may include surgery radiation therapy or chemotherapy when those treatments are used to reduce symptoms such as pain.

source_title: Pain and Cancer Treatment - Side Effects - NCI
source_fact_en: Cancer pain can often be controlled with pain medicine and non-drug approaches.

source_title: Pain and Cancer Treatment - Side Effects - NCI
source_fact_en: Tell your care team how well your pain plan is working because untreated pain can become harder to control later.

source_title: Coronary Heart Disease - What Is Coronary Heart Disease? | NHLBI, NIH
source_fact_en: Coronary heart disease happens when plaque narrows the heart's arteries and reduces the flow of oxygen-rich blood to the heart muscle.

source_title: Coronary Heart Disease - What Is Coronary Heart Disease? | NHLBI, NIH
source_fact_en: For many people coronary heart disease can be prevented or slowed with a heart-healthy lifestyle and medicines.

source_title: Coronary Heart Disease - Symptoms | NHLBI, NIH
source_fact_en: Coronary heart disease may stay silent until it causes a heart attack or another complication.

source_title: Coronary Heart Disease - Symptoms | NHLBI, NIH
source_fact_en: As plaque builds up you may notice chest pain shortness of breath or neck pain during activity and the symptoms may improve with rest.

source_title: Coronary Heart Disease - What Is Coronary Heart Disease? | NHLBI, NIH
source_fact_en: Doctors diagnose coronary heart disease using symptoms medical and family history risk factors and heart tests.

source_title: Coronary Heart Disease - Risk Factors | NHLBI, NIH
source_fact_en: Smoking high blood pressure high LDL cholesterol diabetes obesity and poor sleep can all raise the risk of coronary heart disease.

source_title: Coronary Heart Disease - Symptoms | NHLBI, NIH
source_fact_en: Heart attack pain may feel like pressure squeezing tightness or burning and it can spread to the shoulders arms neck jaw or back.

source_title: Coronary Heart Disease - Symptoms | NHLBI, NIH
source_fact_en: Cold sweats dizziness nausea shortness of breath and weakness can also happen during a heart attack.

source_title: Coronary Heart Disease - Symptoms | NHLBI, NIH
source_fact_en: Women are less likely than men to report classic chest pain during a heart attack and may instead notice dizziness extreme tiredness nausea or stomach pain.

source_title: Coronary Heart Disease - Symptoms | NHLBI, NIH
source_fact_en: If you cannot tell whether chest pain is a heart attack call 9-1-1 right away.
Heart failure symptoms usually get worse as the heart grows weaker.
Shortness of breath during routine tasks such as climbing stairs may be one of the first signs of heart failure.
Left-sided heart failure can cause trouble breathing cough fatigue weakness and difficulty lying flat to sleep.
Right-sided heart failure may lead to swelling in the feet legs or abdomen along with nausea loss of appetite frequent urination or weight gain.
Heart failure can damage the kidneys or liver and can cause fluid to build up in or around the lungs.

source_title: Arrhythmias - What Is an Arrhythmia? | NHLBI, NIH
source_fact_en: An arrhythmia is a problem with the rate or rhythm of the heartbeat so the heart may beat too fast too slow or irregularly.

source_title: Arrhythmias - What Is an Arrhythmia? | NHLBI, NIH
source_fact_en: A frequent irregular rhythm may reduce blood flow and leave you dizzy faint or otherwise unwell.

source_title: Arrhythmias - What Is an Arrhythmia? | NHLBI, NIH
source_fact_en: Untreated arrhythmias can damage the heart brain or other organs and may lead to stroke heart failure or cardiac arrest.
Arrhythmia treatment may include medicines cardioversion catheter ablation pacemakers or implantable defibrillators.

source_title: Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting - Recovery from Surgery | NHLBI, NIH
source_fact_en: After CABG many people stay in the hospital about a week and need roughly 6 to 12 weeks to recover fully at home.

source_title: Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting - Recovery from Surgery | NHLBI, NIH
source_fact_en: Short-term side effects after bypass surgery may include chest pain near the incision constipation poor appetite mood changes sleep problems tiredness or swelling where the graft was taken.

source_title: Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting - Recovery from Surgery | NHLBI, NIH
source_fact_en: After CABG your doctor may prescribe medicines for pain blood pressure cholesterol blood clots or irregular rhythms.

source_title: Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting - Recovery from Surgery | NHLBI, NIH
source_fact_en: Cardiac rehabilitation can help you recover more safely by combining supervised exercise heart-healthy education and stress counseling.

source_title: Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting - Recovery from Surgery | NHLBI, NIH
source_fact_en: If you develop signs of a heart attack after bypass surgery call 9-1-1 right away because a blocked graft can stop blood flow to the heart.
Diabetes occurs when blood glucose also called blood sugar is too high.
The main types of diabetes are type 1 type 2 and gestational diabetes.
Common diabetes symptoms include increased thirst frequent urination tiredness unexplained weight loss and blurred vision.
Some people with diabetes have no symptoms and may not realize they have the disease.
A diabetes care plan should combine healthy habits medicines and blood glucose management in a way that works for you.
The diabetes ABCs focus on A1C blood pressure and cholesterol and quitting smoking is also important.
Managing your diabetes well can lower the risk of heart attack stroke kidney disease blindness and amputations.
You are the most important member of your diabetes health care team.
What you eat how much you eat and when you eat are all important parts of a diabetes meal plan.
Healthy living can help keep blood glucose blood pressure and cholesterol in range and may delay complications that affect the heart kidneys eyes and brain.
If you have overweight or obesity losing 5% to 7% of your current weight may help improve blood glucose blood pressure and cholesterol.
The A1C test shows your average blood glucose level over the past 3 months.
An A1C of 5.7% to 6.4% is used for prediabetes screening and diagnosis.
An A1C of 6.5% or higher can support a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes and usually needs repeat confirmation.
For many people with diabetes the A1C goal is below 7% but personal goals can differ.
Low blood glucose is common in people with type 1 diabetes and in many people with type 2 diabetes who use insulin or certain diabetes medicines.
Hypoglycemia can make you feel shaky hungry tired dizzy confused irritable or as if your heart is beating too fast.
Very low blood glucose can cause seizures or loss of consciousness and needs treatment right away.
Keep a glucagon kit available for severe hypoglycemia and consider wearing medical alert identification.
Diabetic kidney disease often has no symptoms so testing is the only way to know if it is present.
People with type 2 diabetes and people with type 1 diabetes for more than 5 years should be tested every year for kidney disease.
Doctors use blood and urine tests to check for diabetic kidney disease.
Reaching your blood glucose and blood pressure goals is one of the best ways to slow or prevent diabetes-related kidney disease.
Stopping smoking limiting salt staying active and maintaining a healthy weight can help protect your kidneys.
A cataract is a cloudy area in the lens of the eye that can make vision blurry hazy or less colorful.
Cataracts may start without obvious symptoms but over time they can interfere with reading night vision and other daily activities.
Cataract surgery is a common and generally safe operation that can correct vision problems caused by cataracts.

source_title: Causes of Cataracts | National Eye Institute
source_fact_en: Diabetes smoking heavy alcohol use long sun exposure steroids and past eye injury or surgery can raise the risk of cataracts.
Glaucoma usually has no symptoms at first so many people do not know they have it.
Over time glaucoma often causes slow loss of side vision before central vision is affected.
Get urgent help for sudden intense eye pain red eye blurry vision or nausea because angle-closure glaucoma is an emergency.
If you are at higher risk for glaucoma ask how often you need a comprehensive dilated eye exam.
Glaucoma treatment may include prescription eye drops laser therapy or surgery to lower eye pressure.
Treatment cannot reverse vision already lost from glaucoma but it can help stop the damage from getting worse.
Dry eye happens when the eyes do not make enough tears or when the tears do not work well enough.
Dry eye can cause burning scratchiness red eyes blurry vision and sensitivity to light.
Your doctor can check for dry eye during a comprehensive dilated eye exam and may measure tear amount tear stability and eyelid structure.
Treatment for dry eye may include artificial tears prescription eye drops tear-duct plugs or other measures based on the cause.
To ease dry eye try avoiding smoke and wind taking screen breaks using a humidifier drinking water and getting enough sleep.
Diabetic retinopathy damages the blood vessels in the retina and can cause vision loss or blindness in people with diabetes.
Early diabetic retinopathy may have no symptoms even while damage is beginning.
Later diabetic retinopathy can cause blurry vision and dark floating spots or streaks in your vision.
If you have diabetes get a comprehensive dilated eye exam at least once a year.
Managing blood sugar blood pressure and cholesterol can help lower the risk of diabetic retinopathy and related vision loss.

source_title: Get a Dilated Eye Exam | National Eye Institute
source_fact_en: A dilated eye exam is one of the best ways to detect eye disease early before it causes vision loss.

source_title: Get a Dilated Eye Exam | National Eye Institute
source_fact_en: Most people with diabetes or high blood pressure need a dilated eye exam at least once a year.

source_title: Get a Dilated Eye Exam | National Eye Institute
source_fact_en: A dilated eye exam may include tests of visual acuity peripheral vision eye movements pupil response eye pressure and dilation itself.

source_title: Get a Dilated Eye Exam | National Eye Institute
source_fact_en: Your vision may stay blurry and your eyes may feel light-sensitive for a few hours after dilation so sunglasses and a ride home can help.
